`airgap-rag` is plain markdown: `SKILL.md` and the reference files below. The agent reads them and does the work itself; nothing is installed or run.

## Workflow

Copy this checklist into your reply and tick it off as you go:

```
Air-gap RAG:
- [ ] 1. Blueprint read
- [ ] 2. Interview
- [ ] 3. Platform and vector store chosen
- [ ] 4. Extraction and OCR
- [ ] 5. Models
- [ ] 6. Sizing
- [ ] 7. Configuration files
- [ ] 8. Bulk-load runbook and LLM wiki
- [ ] 9. docs/airgap/rag.md
- [ ] 10. Manifest rows
- [ ] 11. Verification steps
- [ ] 12. Self-check, until every item holds
- [ ] 13. Hand-over to airgap-transfer
```

1. **Blueprint.** Read `docs/airgap/blueprint.md` (or the path `AGENTS.md` names) and `docs/airgap/transfer-manifest.md`. Take the vLLM and Open WebUI versions, `org.isolation`, `hardware.gpus` and the `rag` group from them. With no blueprint, ask for them in the interview.
2. **Interview.** Read [`references/interview.md`](/reference/rag/interview/). Ask only the questions the user's message and the blueprint leave open. When the user has not named a platform, ask the platform question with its three options (Open WebUI knowledge bases, recommended; a RAG server, RAGFlow; something else) and wait for the answer, even when they said "set it up", with the other open questions and their defaults in the same message so one reply settles everything. Continue without asking when they named a platform or said to take the recommended option or the defaults; for the other open questions, state the defaults, list them as assumptions in `rag.md` and continue. When the user's answers are short or they ask to go faster, take the fast path: offer the defaults and show the sizing as one summary table.
3. **Platform and store.** Read [`references/decisions.md`](/reference/rag/decisions/) and the catalog entry of each choice. Open WebUI knowledge bases is the default and the recommendation; a standalone RAG server is RAGFlow; something else is recorded as custom, with its version and docs link, every value not in the catalog labeled `unverified`, and the air-gap checklist applied in full.
4. **Extraction.** Read [`references/extraction.md`](/reference/rag/extraction/) and [`catalog/docling-serve.md`](/reference/rag/catalog/docling-serve/). Pick the tier by document type, write the OCR languages, and state the cloud rule with its reason in `rag.md`.
5. **Models.** Read [`references/models.md`](/reference/rag/models/) and the entries of the embedding and reranker models. Write the vLLM commands, the Open WebUI settings with `OFFLINE_MODE`, and the model revisions.
6. **Sizing.** Read [`references/sizing.md`](/reference/rag/sizing/). Step by step, every number sourced or marked `estimate`; on the fast path, one summary table. Never skip it. The volume has no default: without it, put it in the open items.
7. **Configuration.** Write `docs/airgap/rag/`: the Open WebUI settings, the vLLM commands, the docling-serve settings when chosen, the chunking settings, or RAGFlow's `.env` with its egress settings.
8. **Runbook and wiki.** Read [`references/ingestion.md`](/reference/rag/ingestion/) for the bulk load, the periodic update and the CLI queries, with the manual steps marked as manual. Read [`references/wiki.md`](/reference/rag/wiki/) when `consumers` includes coding agents.
9. **rag.md.** Write `docs/airgap/rag.md`: decisions with reasons and alternatives, assumptions (every default used), the sizing, the folder to knowledge base to group map for the user to fill in, serving requirements, the environment variable that holds each key, whether `BYPASS_ADMIN_ACCESS_CONTROL` stays on, open items, the components added to the manifest (the catalog ids, and `airgap-rag` for the row of `rag.md` itself), and the checks to run inside. Say that the Open WebUI API values were read from source at tag v0.13.4.
10. **Manifest.** Add rows to `docs/airgap/transfer-manifest.md` as the table below shows. Do not rewrite the blueprint. Mark every row you add by writing "(from airgap-rag)" after the component in its Component cell, for example `docling-serve` (from airgap-rag). In section 2 the marker goes after the name in the Model cell, and `rag.md` lists exactly the names the marked rows use. In section 3, Component is the catalog id, Version the pinned version, File the file name, Arch `amd64` or `arm64`, URL the direct download URL from the catalog's Packages table (or the project path for a project file), and Publisher checksums the checksum file URL (empty when none); for poppler-utils write "not documented" in Version and URL. Section 7 has no Component column, so append the marker to the step text there. `airgap-transfer` accepts rows so marked, without a blueprint row, when `rag.md` lists their component.
11. **Verification.** Read [`references/verification.md`](/reference/rag/verification/). Put the five checks into `rag.md` and into section 7 of the manifest.
12. **Self-check.** Check every item below; fix what fails and check again.
13. **Hand-over.** Below.


## Pages

- [Interview](/reference/rag/interview/): The eight questions airgap-rag asks, with the default for each, and how the platform question is asked and waited on.
- [Decisions](/reference/rag/decisions/): Which platform and vector store to choose and when: Open WebUI knowledge bases, RAGFlow or a custom choice, and why each alternative is refused.
- [Extraction and chunking](/reference/rag/extraction/): The three extraction tiers, the rule that internal documents never leave the network, OCR languages and the chunking settings.
- [Embedding and reranking models](/reference/rag/models/): How the embedding and reranker models are chosen, served on the network's vLLM and wired to Open WebUI with nothing downloaded at start.
- [Sizing the first load](/reference/rag/sizing/): How long the first load takes and how much space the index needs, step by step, with a fast path.
- [Bulk load, updates and queries](/reference/rag/ingestion/): The runbook for loading a folder into a knowledge base, updating it, granting access and querying it over the API.
- [The LLM wiki](/reference/rag/wiki/): Documents as plain markdown files in a git repository, for coding agents that read files.
- [Verification inside](/reference/rag/verification/): The five checks a person runs inside the network: install, retrieval, OCR per language, access and egress.

## Catalog

One entry per component, each with its pinned version, install, outbound switches and sources.

- [BGE-M3](/reference/rag/catalog/bge-m3/): Multilingual embedding model from BAAI with dense, sparse and ColBERT outputs and an 8,192-token window. The alternative embedding model when the user's languages are not named for Qwen3.
- [BGE Reranker v2 M3](/reference/rag/catalog/bge-reranker-v2-m3/): Multilingual reranker from BAAI that vLLM serves without overrides. The alternative to Qwen3-Reranker, and the one that also runs on TEI.
- [Docling Serve](/reference/rag/catalog/docling-serve/): HTTP service that converts scanned and layout-heavy documents (PDF, Office, images) into markdown with layout, table and OCR models. Open WebUI calls it as its content extraction engine.
- [pgvector](/reference/rag/catalog/pgvector/): PostgreSQL extension that stores embeddings and searches them with HNSW or IVFFlat indexes. Open WebUI's default choice for the vector store in this skill, in the same database engine as the blueprint's `postgresql`.
- [Qdrant](/reference/rag/catalog/qdrant/): Standalone vector database server. The choice for very large corpora, or when the vector store should be its own service instead of an extension inside PostgreSQL.
- [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](/reference/rag/catalog/qwen3-embedding/): Open-weight embedding model from the Qwen team, instruction-aware, served by the network's vLLM. The default embedding model of the skill.
- [Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B](/reference/rag/catalog/qwen3-reranker/): Open-weight reranker from the Qwen team, served by the network's vLLM through `/v1/rerank`. The default reranker of the skill.
- [RAGFlow](/reference/rag/catalog/ragflow/): Standalone RAG server with its own web UI and API, document parsing (DeepDoc) and datasets. The alternative to Open WebUI knowledge bases when scanned or complex PDFs and tables are the core of the corpus.
